extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, researchers, and educated public, early 20th century)
extracted.subtask_description: Summaries and reportage of scientific society meetings, experimental results, and commentary on educational and research practice as published in a scientific weekly journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant eligibility and payment unit for secondary education
rubrics_metrics.description: A uniform grant will in future be paid on pupils between twelve and eighteen years of age who are following an approved curriculum, and the term instead of the year is to be taken as the unit in assessing grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies age range (12–18), requires following an approved curriculum, and changes the accounting unit from year to term for grant assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Augmentation of grants for approved educational experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board is prepared in certain cases to augment the grant due to a school by a further sum towards meeting expense incurred by the school in respect of approved educational experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial support may be increased to cover costs of approved experiments, encouraging experimental work in education and the systematic building up of an evidence base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local initiative and course approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The head teacher and local authorities are to be encouraged to submit to the inspector for approval courses of work designed precisely to suit local needs and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages decentralization: locally designed courses may be acceptable if submitted for inspector approval; favors adaptability to local needs rather than rigid central prescription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basing conclusions upon experiment and observation (science of education)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption of the plan followed in all other scientific work of basing conclusions upon experiment and observation should lead to many improvements and the methodical building up of a science of education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that educational policy and practice should be developed from systematic experiments and observations, analogous to other scientific disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proving causation of canal-ray effects via controls
rubrics_metrics.description: That this was due to the canal rays was proved by closing the apertures in the cathodes by means of aluminium shutters, when rotation could not be produced, as also by subjecting the tube to a powerful magnetic field so as to 'deflect to one side all direct or reflected cathode rays.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of negative controls (closing apertures) and manipulations (magnetic deflection) to attribute observed effects (mill-wheel rotation) specifically to canal rays rather than other agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material-dependent interpretation of experimental results
rubrics_metrics.description: When the vanes of the mill-wheel were of mica, the rotation corresponded with bombardment by cathode rays; whereas, when the vanes were of aluminium, rotation in the contrary direction took place; it was suggested that the heat insulating properties of mica and the high thermal conductivity of aluminium have probably an important bearing on the divergent results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare behavior across different materials and incorporate material properties (thermal conductivity, insulation) into causal interpretation rather than attributing effects solely to the ray type without considering target properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of differential thermocouple measurement to detect localized heating
rubrics_metrics.description: By means of two thermojunctions of Constantan/copper on each side of a mica vane, arranged so as to oppose their E.M.F.'s and connected to a mirror galvanometer, it was shown that under canal-ray bombardment the two sides of a mica vane may acquire differences of temperature amounting to as much as 300°F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ opposing thermojunctions and sensitive galvanometer detection to measure small or localized temperature differences produced by bombardment; methodological note on instrumentation and arrangement to detect differential heating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducing natural phenomena in controlled laboratory models
rubrics_metrics.description: To show that sand-ripples of the sea-shore are produced entirely under water, a glass trough with level sand covered by a foot of water was pushed to and fro on rollers; the motion set the water oscillating and small ridges were soon seen in the sand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recreate the essential physical conditions in a controlled, scaled laboratory setup to isolate the causal mechanism (here, under-water oscillation) instead of relying on surface/edge effects (breakers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement across parameter sweeps and recognition of hysteresis and material differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Wires of steel, iron, platinum, and copper were heated by an electric current of gradually increasing and decreasing strength, and corresponding measurements of Young's modulus made; the return for decreasing currents followed a somewhat similar course, but not coincident with the course during increasing current; in platinum there was no initial decrease for weak currents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform systematic parameter variation (increasing and decreasing) to reveal nonlinearity and hysteresis; compare different materials to note distinct behaviors and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid coarse rounding in divided-circle measurements; use multiple microscope readings
rubrics_metrics.description: Results show that it would be a mistake to limit the use of the division to entire degrees, leaving the remainder to a simple interpretation; this would involve, even in the mean of six microscope readings, errors of more than 0"·3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using divided-circle instruments, do not restrict use to whole-degree divisions; take multiple fine microscope readings and average to reduce systematic error below the cited threshold (~0.3 arcseconds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate and pragmatically accept proxy physical measurements when differences are small
rubrics_metrics.description: The electric conductivity and angles of minimum deviation of ninety samples of sea water were compared with salinity and density; though the physical properties were not exact measures of the chlorine in sea waters, the differences ... were so small that for purposes of oceanography it may be assumed that the values are identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare proposed proxy observables with direct chemical measures; if discrepancies are negligibly small for the intended application (here, oceanography), proxies may be accepted pragmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for choosing a good solar observatory site and appropriate instrumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the conditions which must be fulfilled by a good solar observatory and the practical difficulties in realising these conditions; Kodaikanal, from its steady climatic conditions and its elevation, was probably as well fitted as any observatory; exhibited spectroheliograms, photographs of the sun's disc and marginal prominences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select observatory locations with steady climate and suitable elevation; ensure appropriate instrumentation and methods (spectroheliography, photographic records) and consider practical difficulties in implementation and data interpretation.
